title: BJT Operating Regions Explorer
description: Common-emitter output characteristics of a bipolar junction transistor for a family of base currents, with the saturation, forward active, and cutoff regions shaded, a load line, and the DC operating point. A two-by-two map relates the four operating regions to the bias of the two junctions, and a cross section shows the minority carrier profile in the base. Sliders set the current gain, base current, supply voltage, collector resistor, and Early voltage.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: semiconductor physics
bipolar junction transistor
operating regions

educational.topic: Operating regions and output characteristics of the bipolar junction transistor
learningObjectives: Identify the active, saturation, and cutoff regions on the output characteristics
Determine the DC operating point from the load line intersection
Explain how the Early voltage affects the accuracy of a current mirror
prerequisites: BJT structure, minority carrier transport, and current gain

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with real-time characteristic curves, a load line, an operating-point readout, and two linked diagrams
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe: students predict where the operating point moves, then check the region, junction voltages, and currents
assessmentOpportunities: Compute the operating point by hand and compare with the readout
Find the base current that just saturates the transistor for a given load
Estimate current-mirror error from the Early voltage

equations: Forward active: I_C = beta I_B (1 + V_CE/V_A), r_o = V_A/(beta I_B)
assumptions: I_S = 1e-14 A and beta_R = 1 are fixed
Base driven by an ideal current source
limitations: No series resistance, Kirk effect, breakdown, or current dependence of the gain
Cutoff appears only as the I_B = 0 boundary
The base minority carrier profile is a linear-scale sketch
